checks.claim: C1: Spatial increment map and the descending all-label elimination invariant across two block chains, covering all pairings (crossing and domestic), empty chains and arbitrary orders
checks.reason: After the change to increments, each Green factor G(h_l,y_l) depends only on its own y_l. In block order with separate roots, the position x_j is a sum of increments with labels in [b(j),j]. So x_j depends only on labels <= j, and chain-1 positions never involve chain-2 increments. Invariant: before label l, the remaining pairs are exactly those whose closing label is <= l. This holds at l=2k. Closing label l with pair (i,l): x_l-x_i=y_l+z, and z involves only labels < l (same chain: y_{i+1..l-1}; cross-chain: earlier chain-2 increments minus x_i; l=m+1: z=-x_i). Every other remaining pair has its closing label < l, hence both endpoints < l, so it does not involve y_l. The sup-in-z bound depends only on h_l, so Tonelli removes the pair. Opening label l: its partner is larger, so that pair was already removed. Every remaining pair has its closing label < l, so y_l enters only through G and integrates to h_l. In both cases the invariant passes to l-1. Positions of later labels do depend on y_l, but their covariances are already replaced by h-only bounds. This is the point that rescues the elimination order. The argument uses only label comparisons, so it covers crossing and domestic pairs, adjacent pairs (z=0), m=0 or n=0, and every k. I tested it by hand on (0,2), (1,1) and the G1 white order-four position lists. The bounds c h_1/2 and h_1/2 dominate the exact values c h_1/2 and min(h_1,h_2)/2.

checks.claim: C2: Riesz convolution supremum, Gaussian averaging, white bound G<=1/2 times mass one, pair-dependent widths, no pointwise delta
checks.reason: For even f that is nonincreasing in |y|, the map a -> integral of f over [a,a+2h] has derivative f(a+2h)-f(a). So the integral is maximal at a=-h. Then (1/2)c_alpha times the integral of |y|^{-alpha} over [-h,h] equals c_alpha h^{1-alpha}/(1-alpha), which is exact. For gamma_eps=p_eps*gamma, Tonelli gives the integral of G(h,y)gamma_eps(y+z) dy as a p_eps-average of shifted integrals, which is bounded by the same supremum. In the white case, G<=1/2 and c_delta p_eps has mass c_delta, so the bound is c_delta/2. Both bounds are independent of eps, and the lemma allows a separate eps_e for each pair. So the source's gamma_{2eps} (chen-13, (2.23)) and any eps_j+eps_k Gaussian widths are covered. The lemma is stated for the smoothed integral S_{D,eps}, which is an ordinary nonnegative integral, so no pointwise delta value is used.

checks.claim: C3: Weighted AM-GM with k openings and k closings, nonnegative weights, sum h <= 2t, exact K_sp and k-power, constants independent of degree and time
checks.reason: The weights are 1 at the k openings and 1-alpha at the k closings, with total W=bk. Weighted AM-GM gives the product of h_l^{w_l} <= (sum h/W)^W times the product of w_l^{w_l}, which is <= (2t/(bk))^{bk}(1-alpha)^{(1-alpha)k}. Multiplying by (c_alpha/(1-alpha))^k gives [c_alpha 2^{2-alpha}(1-alpha)^{-alpha}(2-alpha)^{-(2-alpha)}]^k t^{bk}k^{-bk}, which matches K_sp exactly. White case: the product of h_i over openings is <= (2t/k)^k, and with (c_delta/2)^k this gives c_delta^k t^k/k^k with b=1. The constraint sum h <= 2t holds because the increments sum to the two terminal times; for an empty chain the sum is <= t. Interleaving of openings and closings only loosens the maximum, so the inequality holds. K_sp and Z depend only on (alpha, alpha0, c), not on k, m, D, eps, delta or t.

checks.claim: C4: Truncations replaced by the common full kernel before symmetry; why the summed F_k is symmetric when a single matching is not
checks.reason: chen-13 (2.24): gamma^0_delta(u) is Gamma(alpha0)^{-1} times the integral over [0,1/delta] of e^{-lambda|u|}lambda^{alpha0-1}. This is at most the full integral over [0,infinity), which equals |u|^{-alpha0}, and it is nonnegative. So each regularized diagram is bounded by the same integrand with |s_i-s_j|^{-alpha0}. The spatial bound (E:d1-spatial-max) is extracted next. It is a constant independent of s, m, D and the regularization, because sum h <= 2t on every ordered domain. Only after this is the sum over D taken. Any permutation sigma of labels maps Pi_k bijectively, so F_k(s∘sigma)=F_k(s). The block-preserving permutations tile [0,t]^{2k} into m!(2k-m)! congruent copies of the ordered product domain, and ties are null. A single matching's integrand, or one weighted by a D-dependent spatial factor, is not symmetric; the proof never assumes it is (lines 1163-1165).

checks.claim: C5: Ordered-block factor 1/(m!n!), disjoint-pair cube integral, P_k, binomial split sum, all factors 2, no missing Wick coefficient
checks.reason: The integral of |s-r|^{-alpha0} over [0,t]^2 is 2t^{2-alpha0}/((1-alpha0)(2-alpha0)) = Z t^{2-alpha0}. Each matching uses disjoint pairs, so integrating F_k over the cube gives P_k(Zt^{2-alpha0})^k. P_k=(2k)!/(2^k k!) follows from the recursion. The sum over m of 1/(m!(2k-m)!) is 4^k/(2k)!. The product is K^k t^{bk}k^{-bk} * 4^k/(2k)! * (2k)!/(2^k k!) * Z^k t^{(2-alpha0)k} = (2ZK)^k t^{beta k}/(k! k^{bk}), with b+2-alpha0=beta. The source's Wick formula (2.23) has coefficient one per D in Pi_n, and A_k sums the ordered splits m=0..2k, so (m,n) and (n,m) are both counted. Factors of 2 appear in exactly two places: 2^{2k}/2^k=2^k gives the 2 in 2ZK, and the 2t constraint gives the 2^b inside K_sp. Neither is counted twice. As a check, the white order-two bound 2Z versus the exact 2c_0 gives ratio 2(3-alpha0). At alpha0=0, the static order-four bound 4/(2*4)=1/2 is at least the exact 11/540.

checks.claim: C6: Uniform regularized moment inequality -> L1 product limits -> nonnegative full second-moment series, without circularity
checks.reason: Common parameters (eps,delta) in every factor fall under (2.23). Theorem 4.1 (chen-22, (4.2)) gives L2 limits of X_n^{eps,delta} as eps,delta->0+, so E[X_m^{eps,delta}X_n^{eps,delta}] -> E[X_m X_n] by Cauchy-Schwarz. At fixed k there are only finitely many splits, and the bound is uniform, so it passes to A_k(t). E u^2 = sum of A_k is the reviewed P:mixed series. Its summability rests on L:crude-corrected, which does not use the new bound, so there is no circularity. d=1 needs no G_eta limit.

checks.claim: C7: Factorial inequality direction, q-series bound, exact kappa/time/noise scaling, k=0 separately
checks.reason: From k! <= k^k we get k^{bk} >= (k!)^b, hence k! k^{bk} >= (k!)^{1+b} = (k!)^q, which is the correct direction. For q >= 1 and nonnegative terms, the sum of a_k^q is at most (sum of a_k)^q. This gives the sum of z^k/(k!)^q <= exp(q z^{1/q}) for all z >= 0. With z=2ZK_sp t^beta, z^{1/q}=(2ZK_sp)^{1/q}t^{beta/q} and kappa=beta/q=(4-alpha-alpha0)/(3-alpha), consistent with (E:kappa). A_0=1 equals the k=0 series term. The bound holds for every t>0, not only for large t. It is nonsharp.

checks.claim: C8: First-moment calibration constant, Jensen compatibility, static exponent, normalized Riesz-to-white limit
checks.reason: For one chain, sum h <= t, so the lemma applies with t/2, giving K^k t^{bk}2^{-bk}k^{-bk}. The simplex integral of F_k is P_k(Zt^{2-alpha0})^k/(2k)!, and the product is (ZK/2^{b+1})^k t^{beta k}/(k! k^{bk}). Then C1=q(ZK)^{1/q}/2. C2/C1=2*2^{1/q}=2^{(4-alpha)/(3-alpha)}, matching the stated relation. If the bound holds, Theorem T:first's liminf forces L_* <= C1, and 2^{(4-alpha)/(3-alpha)}>2 gives 2C1<C2. This is consistent with Jensen, E u^2 >= (E u)^2. As alpha0 -> 0, kappa -> (4-alpha)/(3-alpha), which is only an exponent calibration. With c_alpha=(1-alpha)/2 (unit mass on [-1,1]), K_sp=2^{1-alpha}(1-alpha)^{1-alpha}/(2-alpha)^{2-alpha} -> 1 as alpha -> 1, matching c_delta=1.

checks.claim: C10: Overall: does it establish G:upper in the stated one-dimensional cases?
checks.reason: I found no gap, hidden conditional hypothesis or unproved regularity step. The argument proves that limsup t^{-kappa} log E u^2 <= C2 < infinity for d=1 with Riesz 0<alpha<1 or white noise. That is G:upper restricted to these cases, with an explicit nonsharp constant.
